A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PENME, with matching authors, core methodology and experiments despite the revised title and format. All 22 pages of v2 and 21 pages of v3, including their appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original model-editing experiments on Counterfact and zsRE, alongside lexical-bias measurements, ablations, runtime measurements and appendix error analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds streaming-edit, downstream-task and long-form generation results in Tables 1–3 and accompanying appendices.

M1.justification: The contrastive projector and thresholded codebook retrieval remain substantively unchanged. V3 Section 9 adds an IKE-style generation procedure: retrieve edited information, combine it with the query in a new prompt, and generate a longer response. V2 treated long-form generation as future work.

E1.justification: V3 adds DAiR-Emotions classification, CNN/DailyMail summarization and RTE entailment. It also evaluates Counterfact long-form generation and frozen-projector streaming edits, including transfer from Counterfact training to zsRE evaluation. The original editing datasets remain.

E2.justification: New Tables 2–3 introduce unedited-model output controls for downstream and long-form performance. Table 1 retains MELO, GRACE, SERAC, MEMIT and FT. IKE supplies the new generation procedure rather than appearing as a separately scored competing editor.

E3.justification: New protocols include streaming with a frozen projector initialized on 2,000 separate Counterfact samples, downstream evaluation on 2,000 examples each for classification and NLI and 1,000 for summarization, and generation fluency/reference metrics. V3 also replaces the explicitly marked 100-sample GRACE zsRE rows with unqualified rows under a 1,000-edit caption; it does not explain how that replacement was performed.

E4.justification: V3 adds tests of frozen-projector transfer to new edit streams, checks for collateral effects on unrelated NLP tasks, and long-form generation case studies. Existing scaling, layer, margin, distance and error analyses largely remain. Figure 9 presents fewer Llama-2 threshold-sensitivity curves than v2.

E5.justification: Runtime uncertainty values and ROUGE confidence-interval reporting are retained unchanged in v2 Tables 3 and 7 versus v3 Tables 5 and 9. No new seed counts, repeated-run information, significance tests or uncertainty-reporting procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds PENMEstream results while retaining the original PENME scores. GRACE’s GPT2-XL zsRE score changes from 0.343 to 0.667 under different reported sample coverage. New Tables 2–3 report downstream preservation and long-form results, including fluency of 611.54 for unedited Llama-2 versus 622.36 with PENME/IKE. T5-small lexical-bias bars also change, approximately 62% versus 47% at layer 2 in Figure 7.

T1.justification: The contrastive loss, nearest-key retrieval rule, threshold construction and editing criteria retain their mathematical substance. Renaming representations and displaying the existing threshold formula as a numbered equation do not introduce new theory. Neither version provides formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: V3 explicitly claims the first adapter-based approach achieving high efficacy in both generalization and locality. V2 claims a novel projection solution without this specific performance-priority assertion. The central lexical-bias, state-of-the-art performance, efficiency and architectural adaptability claims remain.

C2.justification: V3 interprets streaming results as support for a reusable pretrained projector and downstream results as evidence of preserved general capabilities. Appendix I adds the substantive qualification that successful fact insertion can coexist with hallucinated surrounding content. Earlier hyperparameter and threshold limitations largely remain, moving from Appendix H to J.

D1.justification: V3 supplies a PENME code link, explicitly states projector-layer dimensions and string-valued codebook contents, and adds downstream and generation prompt templates plus a 300-token generation limit. Existing hardware, optimizer, training-budget and data-construction details are largely retained; the two-layer architecture was already described in v2 Appendix A.

R1.justification: V3 substantially expands positioning through PRUNE and AlphaEdit, discussing knowledge preservation and sequential-editing tradeoffs, and adds HooK, additional adapter research and contemporaneous WISE. It also relates lexical bias to earlier NLP dataset-bias research. These additions go beyond the accompanying publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method exposition are extensively rewritten. Threshold selection and codebook management become separate subsections, scaling moves from the ablations section into evaluation, and new evaluation sections are integrated. Terminology largely changes from neighbours to irrelevant prompts; the title and author-name spelling also change.

P2.justification: V3 adopts two-column main text, redraws the explanatory schematics, restyles plots and moves v2 Figure 4 to the opening page as Figure 1. Table 1 gains streaming rows, and four new tables present downstream results, generation results, prompts and examples. Figure 6 changes its axis range and styling while retaining its numerical data.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens empirical support by testing frozen-projector editing, preservation of unrelated task performance and long-form output, previously absent or proposed as future work. Code access information, prompts and the hallucination qualification improve usability and interpretation. The gain is limited by incomplete reporting of downstream scoring metrics and long-form evaluation sample sizes and uncertainty.
